tasks.title: Set Up Gemma 4 Integration with Ollama and JSON Output Validation
tasks.description: Establish the Gemma 4 LLM integration via Ollama with robust JSON output parsing and retry logic. This is the critical unblock for the entire pipeline.
tasks.details:
1. Create `backend/llm/ollama_client.py` with httpx async client to communicate with Ollama API at `http://localhost:11434/api`
2. Implement the 3 Gemma 4 prompts as separate functions:
   - `rewrite_content(chunk: str) -> ContentRewriteResult` (Prompt 1)
   - `classify_content(summary: str) -> ClassificationResult` (Prompt 2)
   - `generate_meeting_overview(summaries: list[str]) -> MeetingOverviewResult` (Prompt 3)
3. Each prompt must instruct Gemma 4 to return ONLY valid JSON with no markdown/backticks/preamble
4. Implement JSON parsing with retry logic (up to 2 retries on malformed output)
5. Create Pydantic models for all response types with validation:
   - `ContentRewriteResult`: title (max 10 words), summary (2-4 sentences), decisions[], action_items[], key_figures{amounts[], vote_tallies[], dates[], schools[]}
   - `ClassificationResult`: primary_category (one of 12 slugs), secondary_tags[], urgency (routine|notable|significant), fiscal_impact (bool), affects_schools[]
   - `MeetingOverviewResult`: meeting_overview, top_decisions[3], fiscal_total (nullable), next_meeting_notes (nullable)
6. Add timeout handling (30 second max per call)
7. Create test script that processes a real LCPS agenda item chunk and validates JSON output
tasks.testStrategy: Unit tests with mocked Ollama responses for all 3 prompt types. Integration test with real Ollama instance processing sample LCPS text chunks. Verify JSON parsing handles edge cases (empty arrays, null values, truncated responses). Test retry logic with deliberately malformed responses.

subtasks.title: Create Ollama Client Module with Async httpx Integration
subtasks.description: Implement the core async HTTP client for communicating with Ollama's API at localhost:11434/api/generate endpoint.
subtasks.details: Create `backend/llm/ollama_client.py` with httpx AsyncClient. Configure OLLAMA_BASE_URL (default http://localhost:11434), MODEL_NAME (gemma4:4b), and TIMEOUT (30 seconds) via environment variables. Implement `_call_ollama(prompt, response_schema)` function that makes POST requests to /api/generate with model, prompt, stream=False, and format parameters. Handle response extraction from JSON response['response'] field.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test with mocked httpx responses verifying correct API endpoint, headers, and payload format. Test timeout configuration applies correctly. Test error handling for network failures and non-200 responses.

subtasks.title: Implement Pydantic Response Models with Validation
subtasks.description: Create Pydantic models for all three LLM response types with field validation and type coercion.
subtasks.details: Create `backend/llm/models.py` with: (1) KeyFigures model containing amounts[], vote_tallies[], dates[], schools[] as list[str] with default_factory. (2) ContentRewriteResult with title, summary, decisions[], action_items[], key_figures - add @field_validator for title max 10 words truncation and key_figures dict coercion. (3) ClassificationResult with primary_category (validated against 12 slugs, defaults to 'general'), secondary_tags[], urgency (validated to routine|notable|significant), fiscal_impact (bool), affects_schools[]. (4) MeetingOverviewResult with meeting_overview, top_decisions[] (capped at 3), fiscal_total (Optional), next_meeting_notes (Optional).
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests for each model: verify valid input passes, invalid categories default to 'general', invalid urgency defaults to 'routine', title over 10 words gets truncated, top_decisions over 3 items gets capped. Test JSON serialization/deserialization roundtrip.

subtasks.title: Implement JSON Parsing with Retry Logic
subtasks.description: Create the retry mechanism for handling malformed LLM JSON output with up to 2 retry attempts.
subtasks.details: Implement `_parse_with_retry(prompt, model_class, schema)` async function that: (1) Attempts to call Ollama and parse response as JSON. (2) On json.JSONDecodeError, ValidationError, KeyError, or TypeError, appends a retry suffix to prompt instructing the model to return ONLY valid JSON with no markdown/backticks/preamble. (3) Retries up to MAX_RETRIES=2 times. (4) Raises ValueError with descriptive message including model class name and last error if all attempts fail. The retry suffix should be explicit about the failure reason.
subtasks.testStrategy: Mock Ollama to return malformed JSON on first call, valid JSON on retry - verify retry happens. Mock to always return malformed JSON - verify raises ValueError after 3 attempts. Test each exception type (JSONDecodeError, ValidationError) triggers retry correctly.

subtasks.title: Implement Three Gemma 4 Prompt Functions
subtasks.description: Create the three async prompt functions for content rewriting, classification, and meeting overview generation.
subtasks.details: Implement: (1) `rewrite_content(chunk: str) -> ContentRewriteResult` using PROMPT_1 template that instructs plain-English rewriting with required JSON structure for title, summary, decisions, action_items, key_figures. (2) `classify_content(summary: str) -> ClassificationResult` using PROMPT_2 template listing exact 12 category slugs and requiring primary_category, secondary_tags, urgency, fiscal_impact, affects_schools. (3) `generate_meeting_overview(summaries: list[str]) -> MeetingOverviewResult` using PROMPT_3 template that joins summaries with '---' separator and extracts meeting_overview, top_decisions[3], fiscal_total, next_meeting_notes. Each function passes model_class.model_json_schema() to enable structured output.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration tests with real Ollama instance for each function. Verify ContentRewriteResult contains valid title Ã¢â€°Â¤10 words. Verify ClassificationResult primary_category is one of 12 slugs. Verify MeetingOverviewResult top_decisions has Ã¢â€°Â¤3 items. Test with edge cases like empty input, very long text.

(2) Runs classify_content on the resulting summary. (3) Runs generate_meeting_overview on both summaries. Reports PASS/FAIL for each step and overall result. Exit code 0 on success, 1 on failure.

subtasks.title: Implement Pydantic models with validation for all three response types

subtasks.title: Implement the three Gemma 4 prompt functions with structured JSON output instructions
subtasks.description: Create rewrite_content(), classify_content(), and generate_meeting_overview() async functions with carefully crafted prompts that instruct Gemma 4 to return valid JSON without markdown or preamble.
subtasks.details: Each prompt explicitly instructs the model: 'return ONLY a valid JSON object, no markdown, no backticks, no explanation'. rewrite_content() transforms government meeting chunks into plain English with title/summary/decisions/action_items/key_figures. classify_content() assigns one of 12 category slugs plus urgency and fiscal_impact flags. generate_meeting_overview() synthesizes multiple item summaries into a meeting-level overview with top 3 decisions.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration test each prompt with sample LCPS text verifying returned JSON parses correctly and all required fields are present.

subtasks.title: Add JSON parsing with retry logic for malformed LLM responses
subtasks.description: Implement robust retry mechanism that re-prompts Gemma 4 up to 2 times when initial response is not valid JSON or fails Pydantic validation.
subtasks.details: The _parse_with_retry() function catches json.JSONDecodeError, ValidationError, KeyError, and TypeError exceptions. On failure, it appends a CRITICAL suffix to the prompt emphasizing strict JSON-only output requirements, then retries up to MAX_RETRIES (2) times. After all retries exhausted, raises ValueError with last error details. This handles edge cases where LLM includes markdown code fences or explanatory text around JSON.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test with mocked responses returning invalid JSON on first attempt, valid on retry. Test retry exhaustion raises ValueError with descriptive message.

tasks.title: Build PDF Extractor and Agenda Item Chunker
tasks.description: Create the PDF text extraction pipeline using pdfplumber that splits documents into agenda item chunks suitable for Gemma 4 processing.
tasks.details:
1. Create `backend/pipeline/pdf_extractor.py` using pdfplumber
2. Implement `extract_text(pdf_path: Path) -> list[PageText]` that extracts text page-by-page
3. Create `backend/pipeline/chunker.py` with agenda item detection logic:
   - Detect agenda item headers (e.g., 'Item 5.A', 'Action Item', 'Consent Agenda')
   - Split text on these headers while preserving context
   - Cap each chunk at 2,000 characters
   - Track page_range for each chunk (e.g., 'pp. 12-15')
4. Define `Chunk` dataclass: text, page_start, page_end, detected_header, char_count
5. Handle PDF edge cases: multi-column layouts, headers/footers, page numbers
6. Create `backend/pipeline/downloader.py` using httpx:
   - Download PDFs with browser-like headers
   - Validate MIME type is application/pdf
   - Save to temp directory with hash-based filename
7. Test with real LCPS and Loudoun County PDFs (download samples manually for testing)
tasks.testStrategy: Unit tests with sample PDF files covering various formats (single column, multi-column, with headers). Test chunker produces chunks under 2,000 chars. Verify page range tracking is accurate. Test downloader with mock HTTP responses and real government PDF URLs.

subtasks.title: Create PDF Downloader Module with httpx
subtasks.description: Implement backend/pipeline/downloader.py to download PDF files from government websites with proper headers and validation.
subtasks.details: Create backend/pipeline/__init__.py and backend/pipeline/downloader.py. Implement async download_pdf(url: str) -> Path function using httpx with browser-like User-Agent headers. Validate MIME type is application/pdf. Generate hash-based filename using hashlib.sha256(url.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]. Save to temp directory using tempfile.gettempdir(). Include timeout handling and retry logic with exponential backoff. Add DownloadError exception class for error handling. Follow httpx async patterns established in backend/llm/ollama_client.py.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests with mocked httpx responses for successful download, invalid MIME type rejection, timeout handling, and retry behavior. Integration test with real government PDF URL to verify download works end-to-end.

subtasks.title: Create PDF Text Extractor with pdfplumber
subtasks.description: Implement backend/pipeline/pdf_extractor.py to extract text page-by-page from PDF documents using pdfplumber library.
subtasks.details: Create backend/pipeline/pdf_extractor.py with PageText dataclass containing: page_num (int), text (str), char_count (int). Implement extract_text(pdf_path: Path) -> list[PageText] function using pdfplumber.open(). Handle multi-column layouts by extracting with default settings (pdfplumber handles this reasonably). Strip headers/footers by filtering lines that appear on multiple pages with same content. Handle PDF edge cases: empty pages, scanned images (return empty text), encrypted PDFs (raise PdfExtractionError). Add logging for extraction progress using Python logging module.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests with sample PDF files covering single-column, multi-column layouts, PDFs with headers/footers, empty pages, and edge cases. Verify page numbering is accurate and text extraction preserves readable content.

subtasks.title: Create Chunk Dataclass and Chunker Module
subtasks.description: Implement backend/pipeline/chunker.py with Chunk dataclass and agenda item detection logic to split extracted text into processable chunks.
subtasks.details: Create backend/pipeline/chunker.py with Chunk dataclass containing: text (str), page_start (int), page_end (int), detected_header (Optional[str]), char_count (int). Implement chunk_text(pages: list[PageText]) -> list[Chunk] function. Create regex patterns to detect agenda item headers: r'(?:Item|ITEM)\s*\d+\.?[A-Z]?', r'(?:Action|ACTION)\s+(?:Item|ITEM)', r'(?:Consent|CONSENT)\s+(?:Agenda|AGENDA)', r'(?:PUBLIC|CITIZEN)\s+(?:HEARING|COMMENT)'. Split text on detected headers while preserving 200 chars of context before each split. Cap each chunk at 2,000 characters, splitting mid-chunk if needed. Track page_range (page_start, page_end) for each chunk based on source PageText objects.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests with sample government meeting text containing various agenda header formats. Verify chunks are under 2,000 chars, page ranges are accurate, detected_header captures the correct pattern, and context is preserved across splits.

subtasks.title: Implement Pipeline Coordinator Function
subtasks.description: Create the main pipeline coordinator that orchestrates download, extraction, and chunking into a single async workflow.
subtasks.details: Add process_pdf(url: str) -> list[Chunk] async function to backend/pipeline/__init__.py. This function: 1) Downloads PDF using downloader.download_pdf(), 2) Extracts text using pdf_extractor.extract_text(), 3) Chunks text using chunker.chunk_text(), 4) Cleans up temp file after processing. Add ProcessingResult dataclass with: chunks (list[Chunk]), source_url (str), page_count (int), total_chars (int). Handle errors at each stage with appropriate logging and cleanup. Integrate with SeenDocument model from backend/db/models.py to check if URL was already processed using sha256 hash.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration tests verifying full pipeline from URL to chunks. Test error handling at each stage (download fail, extraction fail, chunking fail). Verify temp files are cleaned up. Test deduplication logic with SeenDocument.

tasks.title: Initialize PostgreSQL Database Schema with Alembic Migrations
tasks.description: Set up PostgreSQL database with all required tables, relationships, indexes, and full-text search triggers using SQLAlchemy ORM and Alembic migrations.
tasks.details:
1. Create `backend/db/models.py` with SQLAlchemy 2.0 models:
   - `Source`: id, name, base_url, source_type (lcps|loudoun), scrape_config (JSONB)
   - `SeenDocument`: id, url, sha256_hash, processing_status (pending|processing|completed|failed), first_seen_at, last_processed_at
   - `Meeting`: id, source_id (FK), meeting_date, title, source_url, source_pdf_url, meeting_overview, top_decisions (ARRAY), fiscal_total, next_meeting_notes, total_items, fiscal_items, processing_status, created_at, updated_at
   - `AgendaItem`: id, meeting_id (FK), title, summary, primary_category (12 enum values), secondary_tags (ARRAY), decisions (ARRAY), action_items (ARRAY), key_figures (JSONB), urgency (enum), fiscal_impact (bool), affects_schools (ARRAY), source_pdf_url, page_range, search_vector (TSVECTOR), created_at
   - `SupportingDocument`: id, meeting_id (FK), title, url, file_type
   - `PipelineRun`: id, started_at, completed_at, status, documents_processed, items_created, errors (JSONB)
2. Create `backend/db/database.py` with async SQLAlchemy engine and session factory
3. Set up Alembic with initial migration
4. Create PostgreSQL trigger for auto-updating search_vector on agenda_items insert/update
5. Add GIN index on search_vector for fast full-text search
6. Create the 12 category enum type in PostgreSQL
tasks.testStrategy: Run Alembic migrations on fresh PostgreSQL instance. Verify all tables created with correct columns, types, and constraints. Test foreign key relationships. Insert sample data and verify search_vector trigger populates correctly. Test full-text search query performance with GIN index.

subtasks.title: Initialize Alembic Configuration and Directory Structure

subtasks.details: Run `alembic init backend/db/migrations` to create the migrations directory. Modify `alembic.ini` to point to `backend/db/migrations` and set `sqlalchemy.url` to read from environment. Update `backend/db/migrations/env.py` to: (1) import async engine from `backend.db.pool`, (2) import Base from `backend.db.models`, (3) configure `target_metadata = Base.metadata`, (4) implement async migration support using `run_async_migrations()` pattern with `asyncio.run()`. Ensure the script works with `asyncpg` driver by using the existing `settings.database_url` from `backend/config.py`.

subtasks.title: Create PostgreSQL Category Enum Type
subtasks.description: Define a PostgreSQL ENUM type for the 12 agenda item categories to replace the current VARCHAR field.
subtasks.details: Create an Alembic migration that: (1) Creates a PostgreSQL ENUM type named `category_enum` with values matching CATEGORY_LABELS keys from `backend/api/schemas.py`: 'schools-education', 'school-construction', 'budget-finance', 'transportation', 'zoning-land-use', 'public-safety', 'policy-governance', 'equity-inclusion', 'technology', 'community-parks', 'personnel', 'general'. (2) Update `backend/db/models.py` AgendaItem.primary_category to use `Enum(CategoryEnum, name='category_enum')` from SQLAlchemy instead of `String(50)`. Create a Python Enum class `CategoryEnum` in models.py mirroring the 12 values. The migration must handle the column type change safely using `ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE ... USING`.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify ENUM type exists in PostgreSQL with `\dT+ category_enum`. Insert test agenda items with valid and invalid category values. Confirm invalid values are rejected by the database constraint.

subtasks.title: Create Initial Database Migration with All Tables
subtasks.description: Generate and refine the initial Alembic migration that creates all six database tables with proper relationships and indexes.
subtasks.details: Run `alembic revision --autogenerate -m 'initial_schema'` to generate migration from existing models in `backend/db/models.py`. Review and refine the generated migration to ensure: (1) Tables created in correct order respecting foreign keys: sources Ã¢â€ â€™ seen_documents Ã¢â€ â€™ meetings Ã¢â€ â€™ agenda_items, supporting_documents Ã¢â€ â€™ pipeline_runs. (2) All indexes from model `__table_args__` are included: ix_seen_documents_url, ix_meetings_board_date, ix_meetings_date, ix_meetings_status, ix_agenda_items_meeting_id, ix_agenda_items_category, ix_agenda_items_urgency, ix_agenda_items_fiscal, ix_agenda_items_search_vector (GIN). (3) CASCADE delete on foreign keys for agenda_items and supporting_documents. (4) Default values and server_default=func.now() for timestamps.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run `alembic upgrade head` on fresh database. Verify all 6 tables exist with `\dt`. Check indexes with `\di`. Verify foreign key constraints with `\d+ agenda_items`. Run `alembic downgrade base` and confirm clean rollback.

subtasks.title: Implement Search Vector Auto-Update Trigger
subtasks.description: Create PostgreSQL trigger function to automatically populate and update the TSVECTOR search_vector column on agenda_items.
subtasks.details: Create an Alembic migration that adds: (1) A PostgreSQL function `update_agenda_search_vector()` that sets `search_vector = setweight(to_tsvector('english', COALESCE(title, '')), 'A') || setweight(to_tsvector('english', COALESCE(summary, '')), 'B') || setweight(to_tsvector('english', COALESCE(array_to_string(decisions, ' '), '')), 'C') || setweight(to_tsvector('english', COALESCE(array_to_string(action_items, ' '), '')), 'C')`. Weight 'A' for title (highest relevance), 'B' for summary, 'C' for decisions/actions. (2) A trigger `agenda_search_vector_trigger` that fires BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE on agenda_items, calling the function. Use `op.execute()` with raw SQL in the migration.
subtasks.testStrategy: Insert a test agenda item with title, summary, decisions. Verify search_vector is automatically populated. Update the item's title and verify search_vector updates. Test full-text search query: `SELECT * FROM agenda_items WHERE search_vector @@ to_tsquery('english', 'budget')` returns expected results.

Update `backend/db/__init__.py` to export init_db, Base, and AsyncSessionLocal.

tasks.title: Implement Web Scrapers for LCPS and Loudoun County Sources
tasks.description: Build scrapers to discover and fetch meeting documents from lcps.org (BeautifulSoup4) and loudoun.gov (Legistar JSON API).
tasks.details:
1. Create `backend/pipeline/scrapers/base.py` with abstract `BaseScraper` class:
   - `discover_documents() -> list[DocumentInfo]`
   - `fetch_document(url: str) -> bytes`
   - Rate limiting: 4-second delay between requests, never parallel
   - Browser-like headers (User-Agent, Accept, etc.)
2. Create `backend/pipeline/scrapers/lcps_scraper.py`:
   - Navigate lcps.org BoardDocs interface
   - Find meeting agendas and attachments
   - Extract meeting date, title, PDF URLs
   - Use BeautifulSoup4 for HTML parsing
3. Create `backend/pipeline/scrapers/loudoun_scraper.py`:
   - Use Legistar JSON API (structured data, no HTML scraping)
   - Fetch Board of Supervisors, Planning Commission meetings
   - Map API responses to DocumentInfo dataclass
4. Create `backend/pipeline/scrapers/playwright_fallback.py` for JS-heavy pages:
   - Headless browser fallback if basic requests blocked
   - Only activated if initial scrape fails
5. Implement deduplication in `backend/pipeline/deduplicator.py`:
   - Check URL against seen_documents table
   - Compute SHA-256 hash of PDF content

6. Define `DocumentInfo` dataclass: url, pdf_url, title, meeting_date, board_type, sha256_hash
tasks.testStrategy: Integration tests against live lcps.org and loudoun.gov (with rate limiting). Mock tests for unit testing scraper logic. Verify deduplication correctly skips already-processed documents. Test Playwright fallback triggers when needed. Validate all discovered documents have required metadata.

tasks.title: Build Complete Pipeline Worker with APScheduler
tasks.description: Create the standalone pipeline worker process that orchestrates scraping, PDF extraction, Gemma 4 processing, and database writes on a 6-hour schedule.
tasks.details:
1. Create `backend/pipeline/worker.py` as the main entry point:
   - APScheduler with IntervalTrigger(hours=6)
   - Run as separate process from FastAPI server
   - Never block on LLM calls
2. Implement full pipeline flow in `backend/pipeline/processor.py`:
   - Step 1: Run all scrapers, collect new documents
   - Step 2: Deduplicate against seen_documents
   - Step 3: Download PDFs, validate MIME types
   - Step 4: Extract text with pdfplumber
   - Step 5: Chunk into agenda items
   - Step 6: For each chunk, call Gemma 4 Prompt 1 (content rewrite)
   - Step 7: For each rewritten summary, call Gemma 4 Prompt 2 (classification)
   - Step 8: Run 10 quality validation checks before DB write
   - Step 9: Atomic PostgreSQL transaction to insert meeting + agenda_items
   - Step 10: After all chunks processed, call Gemma 4 Prompt 3 (meeting overview)
   - Step 11: Update meeting record with overview
3. Create `backend/pipeline/validator.py` with 10 quality checks:
   - Title not empty, under 100 chars
   - Summary between 50-500 chars
   - primary_category is valid slug
   - urgency is valid enum
   - Decisions array not empty for non-routine items
   - Key figures amounts are valid currency strings
   - Vote tallies match pattern (e.g., '5-2')
   - No duplicate agenda items in same meeting
   - Page range format valid
   - Source PDF URL is valid URL
4. Log all pipeline runs to pipeline_runs table
5. Handle errors gracefully: mark documents as failed, continue with next
tasks.testStrategy: End-to-end test with mock scrapers and real Gemma 4. Test APScheduler triggers correctly. Verify atomic transactions rollback on validation failure. Test error handling doesn't crash worker. Verify pipeline_runs table logs all executions.

tasks.title: Create FastAPI REST API with Redis Caching
tasks.description: Build the FastAPI application with all required REST endpoints, Redis caching with 15-minute TTL, and proper error handling.
tasks.details:
1. Create `backend/api/main.py` with FastAPI app initialization
2. Set up async Redis client using redis-py with Upstash connection string
3. Implement cache decorator with 15-minute TTL for read endpoints
4. Create `backend/api/routes/meetings.py`:
   - GET `/api/meetings`: Paginated list (20 per page), newest first, returns meeting summaries
   - GET `/api/meetings/{id}`: Full meeting with all agenda items and supporting documents
5. Create `backend/api/routes/categories.py`:
   - GET `/api/categories`: All 12 categories with item counts
   - GET `/api/categories/{slug}`: Paginated agenda items for one category
6. Create `backend/api/routes/search.py`:
   - GET `/api/search?q=`: PostgreSQL full-text search across title, summary, decisions
